scope: Cloud Linux Chromium software SwiftShader CPU workload in an idle production battle, not an iPhone temperature or power measurement.

summary.scope: Production build, idle battle at a fixed legal engine-generated state; Linux Chromium with explicit software SwiftShader. Browser process CPU comparison only. No real-device GPU power/temperature measurement; results must not be represented as iPhone thermal savings. No battle action/save costs measured.

summary.orderPolicy: Cyclic rotated ordering by repetition; focused 2x2 after disabling background FX to avoid CPU saturation
summary.scope: Focused production idle-battle 2x2: background WebGL FX disabled in all cases, independently stop garden WebP and portrait videos; CSS motion remains enabled. Same fixed legal engine-generated state; Linux Chromium with explicit software SwiftShader. Browser process CPU comparison only. No real-device GPU power/temperature measurement; results must not be represented as iPhone thermal savings. No battle action/save costs measured.

failedInitialHarnessAttempt.error: English browser locale did not match existing Japanese enterGame helper. No measurements were produced.
failedInitialHarnessAttempt.changed: Set browser locale ja-JP; game and comparison conditions unchanged.

supported: Motion reduction greatly lowered cloud browser CPU workload in the primary experiment.

Primary normal rendering saturated almost four CPU cores; a garden-only or portrait-only stop increased background draw throughput instead of lowering total CPU. These are not evidence that the removed components are free.
With background WebGL disabled in all focused conditions, stopping garden WebP reduced median CPU by about 60%, portrait videos by about 19%, and both by about 83%, each against its same-run control.
No game logic, saves, artwork resolution, or public deployment was changed. Interventions only affect disposable profiling browser contexts.
limitations: The runs used different physical runner CPU models (AMD versus Intel); do not directly compare absolute CPU percentages across runs.
Software rendering overstates some CPU costs relative to a phone with a real GPU. Percent reductions must not be treated as iPhone temperature, power or battery savings.
Only three samples per group, 8-second windows after 5-second warmup. CPU scheduling and playback throughput vary.
A fixed ready/idle battle was measured with audio volume muted; attack simulation, long-session leaks, actual phone temperature, charging and screen brightness were not measured.
Stopping all garden WebP together does not identify how much belongs to the frame versus the crystal separately.

reproduction.browserCpuMetric: Sum of Chrome SystemInfo.getProcessInfo CPU time deltas divided by measured wall time. 100% means one full core; four logical cores can approach 400%.
